paragraphs: Postsecondary art, drama and music teachers (corresponding on the US side to O*NET/BLS 25-1121.00 Art, Drama, and Music Teachers, Postsecondary) teach drama, music and art courses to undergraduate and graduate students, covering both those mainly teaching and those combining teaching and research; the respondent job titles listed on the page include Art History Professor, Art Instructor, Art Professor, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Instructor, Music Instructor, Music Professor, Professor and Theater Professor. Daily tasks include preparing and teaching courses in performance fundamentals, music theory, art history and studio practice for undergraduate and graduate students; preparing course materials (syllabi, assignments and lecture notes); organising and directing rehearsals and performances and exhibitions; marking assignments and works and grading; supervising students' graduation works and rehearsal and performance practice; conducting art history and theory and work research; publishing or performing results in the field and attending professional conferences; writing funding applications and reviewing others' applications; maintaining fixed office hours to tutor students; planning, evaluating and revising course content and teaching methods; keeping records such as attendance and grades; taking part in student recruitment and employment guidance; reviewing for professional journals and monographs; participating in campus and community activities and academic committee work; taking on administrative duties such as department chair; serving as adviser to student organisations; compiling subject bibliographies; and providing professional consulting for government or industry. Under the Occupational Classification Code of the People's Republic of China (2022 edition), the closest national occupation is higher education teacher under the teaching personnel sub-category (this page does not provide an unverified detailed category code); under the Higher Education Law of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications, teaching in a higher education institution requires obtaining a higher education teacher qualification; Article Forty-Six of that law provides that a person with graduate or university undergraduate education, with corresponding teaching and learning ability and who has been assessed as qualified, may obtain a higher education teacher qualification, and Article Forty-Seven provides that teacher positions are set as teaching assistant, lecturer, associate professor and professor (specific exemption cases are subject to the rules of the institution and the education administrative department). This page does not constitute legal, hiring or professional title review opinion.

Three small self-assessable tasks: write the syllabus outline for a 90-minute undergraduate course (learning objectives, reading materials, class activities, assessment method and time allocation); use fictional material to complete a grading and feedback report on a work or performance (grading rubric, comments and improvement suggestions); write a two-page statement to a funder for a creative or research project you plan to undertake (creative or research question, gaps in existing work, method and expected contribution). (Editorial suggestion, not a hiring, professional title review or teaching ability test, and it does not constitute a description of any institution's process.)

People more likely to adapt: willing to teach and demonstrate to students over the long term and to accept public expression and being evaluated; able to arrange time among teaching, creation and research and practical performance (48% of respondents work more than 40 hours per week and 9% have irregular schedules); able to keep producing verifiable works or research results and to withstand competition in performance, exhibition, publication and funding (21% extremely competitive, 26% highly competitive); and willing to guide students and practice according to academic and creative norms and ethics. If you are unwilling to teach publicly over the long term and accept evaluation by students and peers, find it hard to keep advancing creation and research with self-arranged time, are unwilling to record grades and supervision processes to standard, or are unprepared psychologically for competition over works and funding, the risk is usually greater.

US wages and employment on this page are BLS data shown by O*NET (occupation-specific measure for postsecondary art, drama and music teachers): 2025 median annual wage 78,620 US dollars (10th percentile 47,570, 25th percentile 61,620, 75th percentile 103,850, 90th percentile 163,350 US dollars; no hourly wage is provided on the page), about 122,800 employed in 2024, 2024—2034 below-average growth of 1% to 2%, about 9,000 openings per year; the main industry is educational services (100% of employment in this occupation). The BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook entry Postsecondary Teachers is a combined measure (covering postsecondary teachers in all subjects): about 1,378,200 jobs in 2025, 7% growth for 2025—2035 (much faster than average), a ten-year net increase of about 98,200, and about 103,300 openings per year; the combined figure cannot be used as a separate figure for this occupation. Mainland China has no precise national wage distribution for this occupation, and industry sector figures serve only as a broad reference; teaching in a higher education institution requires obtaining a higher education teacher qualification under the Higher Education Law of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications. This page does not constitute legal or hiring opinion.

In one sentence: a teaching-and-research role in higher education that teaches the knowledge and techniques of drama, music and art to undergraduate and graduate students while deepening art practice through creation, performance, research and student supervision.

The work of postsecondary art, drama and music teachers can be divided into four categories: teaching and curriculum building (preparing lecture notes and course materials, teaching courses such as research methods, studio art, performance practice, language and culture to undergraduate and graduate students, leading class discussions, marking assignments and papers and grading, planning, evaluating and revising course content and teaching methods, and compiling subject bibliographies); supervising students (maintaining fixed office hours to tutor students, supervising theses and internships and research, supervising students' studio and rehearsal and performance practice, guiding undergraduate and graduate teaching and research work, writing recommendation letters, and serving as adviser to student organisations); research and academic output (conducting art history and theory and work research and special studies, publishing results in professional journals and monographs and performances and exhibitions and academic conferences, writing funding applications and reviewing others' applications, reviewing for art and performance journals and monographs, and working with colleagues to solve teaching and research problems); and administration and professional service (taking part in departmental and university-level committees and institutional affairs, taking on administrative duties such as department chair, participating in student recruitment and registration and employment placement, participating in campus and community activities, providing professional consulting for government or industry, and attending academic conferences to keep up with the field).

O*NET25-1121.00 teaches drama, music, fine art, applied art, design and craft, covering both those focused mainly on teaching and those combining teaching and research. The current 30 tasks comprise 20 core, 8 supplementary and 2 unscored new tasks (directing theatre productions and tutoring students), and unscored tasks are not treated as meaning no duty. Job Zone Five/SVP8 and above is a preparation zone description; the education survey for this occupation shows master's 51%, doctorate 32% and bachelor's 14%, which is not an individual admission proportion or a uniform national requirement. The interest code SA describes work tendencies, not an individual competency conclusion.

entries: Teaching and curriculum building｜Explaining the subject and techniques clearly｜Preparing and teaching drama, music and art courses for undergraduate and graduate students, preparing syllabi and assignments and lecture notes and repertoire and plays, initiating and leading class discussions and studio and rehearsal activities, and planning, evaluating and revising course content and teaching methods.

Assessment and feedback｜Grading to standard and giving improvement suggestions｜Writing, administering and marking exams and work and performance assessments, reviewing assignments and works and grading, and following the grading standard and stating the basis and improvement direction in comments.

Supervising students｜Supporting learning and research according to the division of labour｜Maintaining office hours, tutoring courses, internships, research and rehearsals, and providing academic and career advice; no recommendation-letter duty is added from the current task list.

Creation and research and publication｜Some roles carry research｜Supplementary tasks include conducting research in the field and publishing in professional journals, books or electronic media; journal peer review is not written as a duty verified this time.

Funding and collaboration｜Some roles apply for research support｜Writing funding applications, collaborating with colleagues on teaching and research, reading material and attending professional conferences to keep up; the tasks this time do not support reviewing others' funding applications.

Administration and professional service｜Supporting the operation of the department and discipline｜Participating in academic and administrative committees dealing with institutional, departmental, academic and performance matters, taking on administrative duties such as department chair, participating in student recruitment and registration and employment placement and campus and community activities, and providing professional consulting for government or industry.

The weight of the four task categories differs by institution type (research universities, teaching-oriented institutions and community colleges): research universities emphasise research output and graduate supervision more, teaching-oriented institutions emphasise teaching hours and undergraduate teaching more, and community colleges focus mainly on teaching and usually do not require research output; the same title may differ greatly in actual requirements across institutions.

The 2025 occupational annual wage P10/25/50/75/90 is 47,570/61,620/78,620/103,850/163,350 US dollars, with no hourly wage given; percentiles are not starting salaries. Current 2025 employment is 116,900, the 2025—2035 growth category is 1% to 2%, and average annual openings are 8,000; the BLS detailed row shows 2.2% growth and a net increase of 2,600, rounded to 2% in the OOH. The industry page shows educational services 100% with no separate statistical year; the US associated unique hiring software for 2025 shows PS3%, Illustrator2%, CreativeCloud2%, and Office/InDesign/AfterEffects 1% each, which is not an adoption rate.

Set course and performance goals: state learning objectives and assessment methods and performance requirements. → Prepare materials: write the syllabus and lecture notes and rehearsal plan and repertoire and plays. → Deliver teaching: teach and demonstrate techniques and lead discussion and rehearsal. → Assess and give feedback: grade to standard and give improvement suggestions. → Supervise students: answer questions and guide graduation works and rehearsals and performances. → Advance creation and research: perform or publish results and apply for funding and revise the course.

National Bureau of Statistics, Average Annual Wages of Urban Unit Employees in 2025 (released 2026-05-15): national urban non-private units 129,441 yuan per year, urban private units 71,590 yuan per year; employees of above-scale enterprises 106,080 yuan per year, of whom professional and technical personnel 155,491 yuan per year and clerical and related personnel 94,936 yuan per year; by industry sector (urban non-private units) education 133,539 yuan per year, culture, sports and entertainment 129,447 yuan per year, scientific research and technical services 182,064 yuan per year, and public administration, social security and social organisations 119,465 yuan per year. None of the sectors and job categories above list this occupation separately and they serve only as a broad reference.

Teaching records (syllabi, grades and attendance, comments and feedback, supervision records) and research records (research data, interview and studio practice records, manuscripts and review comments) are the basic material for making the teaching and academic process verifiable and traceable; where student grades and identity information, unpublished works and creative records and participant information are involved, they must be kept and handled according to institution and ethics committee requirements and must not be shared externally at will; citing others' works and materials and data requires stating the source.

Occupation-specific: current O*NET 2025 employment 116,900, 2025—2035 growth category below average at 1% to 2%, average annual openings 8,000, including growth and replacement. The BLS detailed occupational table shows 2.2% growth over the same period, 119,500 employed in 2035 and a net increase of 2,600; the OOH presents it as 2% in whole numbers. The postsecondary teachers combined figure of 1,378,200, 7%, net increase 98,200 and annual average 103,300 is still a combination including all subjects and cannot be used as the value for this occupation.

Prepare the lesson: state learning objectives and reading and activity arrangements. → Teach: lecture and lead discussion and questions. → Office hours: tutor students at fixed times and keep records. → Grade: grade to the rubric and write comments and improvement suggestions. → Supervise: guide student theses and studio and rehearsal and performance practice. → Review: revise the course based on student feedback and research progress.

Article 46 of China's Higher Education Law implements the higher education teacher qualification system: qualifying education, teaching and learning ability and assessment; those without the listed education but with a strong command of their field, who pass the national teacher qualification examination and are assessed as qualified, may also obtain it. Articles 47/48 separate teacher positions and appointment. Articles 2/4 of the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications require a qualification specifically for teaching and learning and make the higher education qualification independent; Article 11 requires two professors or associate professors to recommend an applicant for the examination, and not all qualification assessments require this material; Article 13 specifies the assessment authority for commissioned higher education institutions and those not commissioned. The complete entries of the occupational code were not read this time, and no one-to-one detailed category is signed off; specific employment education and local assessment requirements should be verified separately.

Teaching and supervision records, assessment and evaluation records, and research data and manuscripts and review records should be kept truthfully according to institution and journal standards with versions and dates noted, so that the work process is verifiable and traceable; scores, attendance and supervision records must not be falsified, research data must not be fabricated or altered, and the content of unpublished works must not be disclosed in peer review.

The boundary comes down to four things: who is responsible for teaching and assessment, who is responsible for creative and research judgement, who is responsible for institutional administration and policy decisions, and who is responsible for awarding students' degrees and managing student status. Postsecondary art, drama and music teachers design courses and deliver teaching and assessment, conduct creation or research and publish or perform results, and supervise students and give academic advice within their duties; degree awarding and student status management and credit recognition are decided by the institution according to its rules; teacher appointment and professional title review are carried out by the institution and review bodies according to regulations; public performances and exhibitions must be carried out in venues meeting safety and authorisation requirements and according to procedure. Teaching content and creative or research conclusions cannot replace the institution's administrative decisions or legal judgement, and matters involving academic and creative misconduct, ethical disputes or major student interests must be reported through institutional procedure.
Complete course design and teaching and assessment, student supervision and research output within the scope of duty, and deliver verifiable teaching and academic records.

Answer questions about teaching and academic delivery with: what are the teaching objectives and assessment standards, whether students have met the learning objectives, whether the creative process and work statement are verifiable, and whether academic and creative norms and ethical requirements are met.

Adjacent duties (artists' creation of works, public education and community engagement by museums and art institutions, student status and degree management by institutional administrative offices, and teacher appointment formalities by human resources) are not counted as core tasks of this occupation.

The objects are the learning and subject knowledge of undergraduate and graduate students and the person's own research questions; the basis is disciplinary theory and methods and pedagogy, the institution's curriculum and assessment rules and academic norms, research ethics and student information protection requirements, and provisions such as the Higher Education Law of the People's Republic of China.

Postsecondary art, drama and music teachers teach drama, music and art courses in higher education and combine teaching with creative or research practice: preparing lecture notes and course materials, organising class discussions and studio and rehearsal activities, assessing and grading assignments and works and performances, supervising students' graduation works and rehearsals and performances, conducting art history and theory and work research, publishing or performing results and applying for funding, and taking on student supervision and academic and administrative service. On the mainland China side the closest national occupation is higher education teacher under the teaching personnel sub-category of the Occupational Classification Code of the People's Republic of China (2022 edition) (this page does not provide an unverified detailed category code), and teaching in a higher education institution requires obtaining a higher education teacher qualification under the Higher Education Law of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications; US wages and employment use the occupation-specific measure shown by O*NET (2025 median annual wage 78,620 US dollars, about 122,800 in 2024, 2024—2034 below-average growth of 1% to 2%, about 9,000 openings per year), and the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook Postsecondary Teachers combined measure (about 1,378,200 jobs in 2025, 7% growth for 2025—2035) is labelled separately.

Learning management systems and online teaching tools, reference management and statistical analysis software, and geographic information systems and imaging and recording equipment can be used for course delivery and material organisation and research analysis, but setting learning objectives and assessment standards and grading judgement, research questions and conclusions, and judgement of academic norms remain the teacher's responsibility and must be recorded truthfully; tool output cannot replace teaching and academic judgement.
Set course objectives → Prepare materials → Deliver teaching → Assess and give feedback → Supervise students → Advance research and revise the course.

Assessed by whether learning objectives are met, whether grading and feedback follow standards and are substantiated, whether the creative process and work statement are verifiable, whether academic and creative norms and ethical requirements are met, and whether student supervision records are complete; not by a single teaching evaluation score or a single paper.

Syllabi and lecture notes and assignments, exam papers and grading rubrics and comments, student supervision and office-hour records, recommendation letters and supervision records, research data and rehearsal and performance records, papers and conference reports and review records, funding applications and project completion material, and course evaluation and improvement records.

Responsibilities are divided according to teaching and research duties and institutional rules; before starting, the role's teaching workload and research assessment requirements, appointment and promotion conditions, safety and ethical requirements for supervising students and studio and rehearsal and performance practice, rules on managing student personal information and unpublished works, and compliance requirements for the use of funds and external consulting should be verified.

Course design and teaching and assessment are borne by the teacher; academic research judgement and responsibility for results are borne by the researcher; degree awarding and student status and credit recognition are decided by the institution according to regulations; teacher appointment and professional title review are the responsibility of the institution and review bodies; public performances and exhibitions must implement safety review and work authorisation according to venue and institutional rules.

Mainland China side: entering a higher education teaching post usually requires a graduate degree in art, drama, music or a related field, and research universities mostly require a doctorate plus creative or published output, while some teaching-oriented institutions and higher vocational colleges accept a master's; teaching in a higher education institution requires obtaining a higher education teacher qualification under the Higher Education Law of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications (a graduate or university undergraduate education and a pass in the teaching and learning ability assessment are required, and the specific exemption and assessment arrangements are subject to the rules of the institution and the education administrative department). On the US side O*NET shows that this occupation requires extensive preparation (Job Zone Five, SVP 8.0 and above), with most roles requiring a graduate degree (some requiring a master's and some a doctorate), and employers usually prefer candidates with teaching experience and a record of works or publications. This page does not provide specific hiring conditions or promotion ratios.

Teaching and research must follow academic and creative norms and ethical requirements: teaching and research involving student personal information and unpublished works must pass institutional ethics and data compliance review; citing others' works and materials and data requires stating the source, and works, data and scores must not be fabricated or altered; student works and personal information and unpublished works must be kept confidential according to rules; academic and creative misconduct and conflicts of interest must be declared and handled through institutional procedure.

When grading records are found not to match the original material, the source of a work or creative process cannot be verified, ethical disputes or conflicts of interest are involved, or a student raises a major objection about grades or supervision, the matter should be paused, the original records retained, and review and reporting carried out through institutional procedure, and records or conclusions must not be altered because of teaching progress or assessment pressure.

Teaching effects and research conclusions apply only to specific course conditions, student groups, materials and methods; the same teaching method or theory may work differently in different institutions and classes, and a single teaching evaluation result must not be presented as a general conclusion, nor preliminary research results presented as a confirmed disciplinary finding.
Work pattern (48% of respondents work more than 40 hours per week, 9% have irregular schedules, 16% sit more than half the time, and it includes public lecturing (60% daily))
Look at the role type and assessment requirements, not the job title.

Role type: research university (mainly research and graduate supervision), teaching-oriented institution (mainly undergraduate teaching), community college (mainly teaching, usually without a research output requirement), and part-time or lecturer post (appointed by course); workload, assessment and stability differ greatly across types.
Education and qualification requirements determine whether one can apply and be appointed.

Education and qualification: whether a doctorate is required, whether a higher education teacher qualification must be obtained (the Higher Education Law of the People's Republic of China requires graduate or university undergraduate education and a pass in the teaching and learning ability assessment, and a pass in the teaching and learning ability assessment), and whether teaching experience or a publication record is required.
The assessment and promotion system directly determines work intensity and career stability.

Assessment and promotion: the appraisal standard for the appointment period (teaching hours, teaching evaluation, papers and projects), whether there is an up-or-out arrangement, the conditions for professional title review and post promotion, and the renewal rules for part-time and lecturer posts.
The time allocation between teaching and research and the competitive pressure affect long-term sustainability.

Work pattern: 48% of respondents work more than 40 hours per week and 9% have irregular schedules, with teaching, creation and research and practical performance coexisting; 21% consider competition extremely intense and 26% highly competitive, and competition in performance, exhibition, publication and funding directly affects appraisal results, which must be checked against the actual contract and appraisal method.
Degree level, publication record and project experience determine long-term development and income level.

Development path: whether one can complete a doctorate and postdoctoral training, keep publishing and lead projects, pass the appointment-period appraisal and professional title review, or move into teaching-oriented institutions, research institutions, museums and art institutions and cultural heritage management, and policy and consulting directions.
Check official and institutional requirements first, then decide on the investment.

Rely on the institution's public recruitment and professional title review documents and the education administrative department's rules on teacher qualification assessment, verify whether the education and qualification and teaching experience channels are compliant, and do not trust unofficial agencies' promises of guaranteed admission, guaranteed appointment to an authorised staff position or guaranteed title review.

paragraphs: Suggested order of choice: first decide the role direction (a teaching-and-research post at a research university, a teaching post at a teaching-oriented institution or community college, or a practical training post focused on art and performance practice teaching), then verify the education and qualification requirements (whether a doctorate is required, whether a higher education teacher qualification must be obtained under the Higher Education Law of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications, and whether institutional pre-service teacher training and teaching and learning ability assessment are required), and finally confirm the teaching and creative conditions, the assessment and promotion system, the work pattern and the pay and benefits structure. All directions share course design, lecturing, assessment and student supervision ability; moving to an adjacent occupation requires building different abilities and output forms (textual and field research and cultural analysis, field investigation and research on remains and objects, spatial design and construction technology, and information organisation and library services), and the duty systems differ, so it cannot be transferred directly.

The basis for comparison is O*NET 25-1121.00, the BLS 2025 wage percentiles and 2024—2034 employment projection shown by O*NET, the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook Postsecondary Teachers (combined measure), the higher education teacher entry under the teaching personnel sub-category of the Occupational Classification Code of the People's Republic of China (2022 edition), and public material such as the provisions of the Higher Education Law of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications on higher education teacher qualifications and the teacher position and appointment system; the adjacent occupation section is used only to explain boundaries and does not mean qualifications or duties can be transferred between them.

The table below compares three directions within this occupation and three adjacent occupations, using the same comparison dimensions: direction, core work and output, key differences, and what choice it suits better.
Teaching and creation carry equal weight; creative or research output and funding and graduate supervision are the core of appraisal, and appointment-period pressure is the greatest.
People willing to do original creation or research over the long term while also taking on teaching and graduate supervision.

Teaching undergraduate and graduate courses, supervising graduation works and rehearsals and performances, independently conducting art history and theory and work research or creation and publishing or performing in journals and monographs and performances and exhibitions, applying for funding and taking part in academic and artistic service.

Mainly teaching; teaching hours are heavier and class sizes larger, and creative or research output is usually not the main appraisal basis.
People more willing to put their energy into classroom teaching and student tutoring and rehearsal guidance rather than publication or public performance.
Designing teaching and assessment for foundation courses, delivering classroom and studio and rehearsal teaching, and taking on student tutoring and course improvement.
Teaching-oriented institution and community college teaching post direction

Mainly art and performance practice teaching; studio, rehearsal and performance training must be organised according to institutional and venue requirements, and safety and work authorisation requirements are the highest.
People willing to lead students in studio and rehearsal and performance training over the long term and to take responsibility for safety and compliance.

Guiding students in studio and rehearsal and performance training, demonstrating techniques and rehearsal and show organisation methods, reviewing the quality of student works and rehearsal records, and organising training assessments.
Art and performance practice teaching direction

Studying the history and culture of regions and ethnic groups through textual and field material; the material is mainly textual and field records; it does not carry this occupation's art and performance course and assessment duties.
People more willing to study culture and people through textual and field material.
Teaching area and ethnic studies courses, conducting textual and field research and supervising theses.
Postsecondary area, ethnic and cultural studies teachers (adjacent occupation)

Mainly uses field investigation and material culture and remains as material; compared with this occupation it relies more on objects and field records, and the teaching duty structure is similar but the disciplinary object differs.
People more willing to do field investigation and research on objects and remains.
Organising field investigation and material organisation and analysis, teaching anthropology and archaeology courses and supervising theses.
Postsecondary anthropology and archaeology teachers (adjacent occupation)

Also uses the design studio and work critique teaching method, but the output is architectural and spatial schemes and technical drawings; it does not carry drama and music course and performance direction duties.
People more willing to do spatial and construction design and lead a design studio.
Teaching architecture and construction courses, leading the design studio and work critique and supervising graduation design.
Architecture teachers (higher education) (adjacent occupation)

After deciding the direction, verify the education and qualification requirements that actually exist for each direction (whether a doctorate is required, whether a higher education teacher qualification must be obtained under the Higher Education Law of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications, and whether institutional pre-service teacher training and teaching and learning ability assessment are required), the appointment-period appraisal and promotion system, and the safety and work authorisation requirements for studio and rehearsal and performance training.

entries.answer: Preparing lecture notes and course materials and teaching drama, music and art courses to undergraduate and graduate students (such as performance fundamentals, music theory, art history and studio practice, including fine art and applied art and design and craft); leading class discussions, marking assignments and papers and grading; maintaining fixed office hours to tutor students, supervising theses and studio and rehearsal practice; conducting art history and theory and work research and publishing results in journals and monographs and performances and exhibitions; writing and reviewing funding applications; taking part in academic and administrative committees and departmental management, participating in student recruitment and campus activities, and providing professional consulting for government or industry.

entries.answer: Postsecondary area, ethnic and cultural studies teachers design courses and deliver teaching and assessment, supervise students and conduct research and publish results within their duties; degree awarding and student status and credit recognition are decided by the institution according to its rules; teacher appointment and professional title review are carried out by the institution and review bodies according to regulations; postsecondary area, ethnic and cultural studies teachers study the history and culture of regions and ethnic groups through textual and field records, postsecondary anthropology and archaeology teachers use field investigation and remains and material culture as their main material, and architecture teachers (higher education) focus on spatial and construction design and design studio teaching; these adjacent occupations do not carry this occupation's drama and music and art course and performance direction and assessment duties, and their methods and materials differ, so they cannot substitute for each other.

entries.answer: Look at observable behaviour: whether you can lecture publicly in class over the long term and accept student evaluation and teaching evaluation (60% public speaking every day), whether you can keep advancing creation and research writing under self-arranged time (48% work more than 40 hours per week, 9% irregular schedules), whether you can grade to standard and give executable feedback, and whether you can keep producing verifiable results under publication and funding competition (21% extremely competitive, 26% highly competitive). entries.answer: Mainland China side: teaching in a higher education institution requires obtaining a higher education teacher qualification under the Higher Education Law of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications; Article Forty-Six of the Higher Education Law provides that a person with graduate or university undergraduate education, with corresponding teaching and learning ability and who has been assessed as qualified, may obtain a higher education teacher qualification, Article Forty-Seven provides that teacher positions are set as teaching assistant, lecturer, associate professor and professor, and Article Forty-Eight provides for a teacher appointment system; Article Four of the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications lists the higher education teacher qualification as an independent category, Article Eleven provides that the examination is held as needed and requires two professors or associate professors in a related major to recommend the applicant, and Article Thirteen makes clear that commissioned higher education institutions are responsible for the assessment. On the US side O*NET shows no uniform licensing requirement for this occupation, and institutional and accrediting body requirements dominate, usually requiring a related master's or doctoral degree and a record of works or research publications. Education, qualification, post hiring and appointment arrangements must be verified separately.

entries.answer: Common misconceptions include: that higher education teachers only teach (in fact teaching runs in parallel with creation or research and administrative service, with 48% working more than 40 hours per week); that classroom and studio teaching can be without standards (in fact safety norms and work and material verification are needed, and simplifying complex art and performance experience into stereotypes harms students); that a degree alone earns tenure or course autonomy (in fact appointment and tenure are decided by institutional rules); that there is a uniform licence (on the US side O*NET shows no uniform licensing requirement, and on the mainland China side a higher education teacher qualification must be obtained); and that performance and exhibition and work use need no authorisation (student personal information and unpublished works require authorisation and review).

subject.name: Postsecondary art, drama and music teachers
subject.summary: Postsecondary art, drama and music teachers teach drama, music and art courses in higher education and combine teaching with creative or research practice: preparing lecture notes and course materials, organising class discussions and studio and rehearsal activities, assessing and grading assignments and works and performances, supervising students' graduation works and rehearsals and performances, conducting art history and theory and work research, publishing or performing results and applying for funding, and taking on student supervision and academic and administrative service; the respondent job titles listed on the O*NET 25-1121.00 page include Art History Professor, Art Instructor, Art Professor, Assistant Professor, Associate Professor, Instructor, Music Instructor, Music Professor, Professor and Theater Professor. On the mainland China side the closest national occupation is higher education teacher under the teaching personnel sub-category of the Occupational Classification Code of the People's Republic of China (2022 edition) (this page does not provide an unverified detailed category code); under the Higher Education Law of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations on Teacher Qualifications, teaching in higher education requires obtaining a higher education teacher qualification, teacher positions are set as teaching assistant, lecturer, associate professor and professor, and a teacher appointment system is applied. US wages and employment use the occupation-specific BLS measure shown by O*NET (2025 median annual wage 78,620 US dollars, about 122,800 employed in 2024, 2024—2034 below-average growth of 1% to 2%, about 9,000 openings per year), while the BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook entry Postsecondary Teachers is a combined measure (about 1,378,200 jobs in 2025, 7% growth for 2025—2035); the two measures and data periods differ and are labelled separately.
